questions.question: With which neighbouring country does India share most of the western border?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India shares most of its **western border** with** Pakistan.**
 
• The border between India and Pakistan is about **3,323 km long** and is known as the** Line of Control (LoC).**
 
• India and Pakistan have a long-standing territorial dispute over the region of **Jammu and Kashmir**, which has led to several conflicts and tensions between the two countries.
 
• The border between India and Pakistan is **heavily guarded** by both sides and is considered to be one of the** most militarized borders **in the world.
 
• The **Wagah border** crossing, located near the city of Amritsar in India and Lahore in Pakistan, is the only road border crossing between the two countries and is a **popular tourist attraction.**
 
• **Myanmar, Bhutan, and China** are India's other neighbouring countries, with whom it shares its **eastern, northern, and northeastern borders**, respectively.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Myanmar** (formerly known as Burma) is a **Southeast Asian **country that shares a** 1,643 km** long border with India.

 
 
• The border between India and Myanmar is known as the** Indo-Myanmar border **and is located in the** northeastern states **of India.
 
 
 
• **Bhutan** is a small landlocked country located in the** eastern Himalayas,** which shares a** 699 km long** border with India.
 
 
• The border between India and Bhutan is known as the** Bhutan-India border **and is located in the northeastern states of India.
 
 
 
• **China** is a neighbouring country located in the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, which shares a** 3,488 km long** border with India.
 
 
• The border between India and China is known as the** Line of Actual Control (LAC) **and is located in the northeastern states of India.
 
• India and China have a longstanding territorial dispute over the** region of Arunachal Pradesh,** which has led to several conflicts and tensions between the two countries.

questions.question:
Which of the following factors affect distribution of population?

I. Climate

II. Soil

III. Topography

IV. Water
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II, III, and IV.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Factors like **climate, soil, topography, and water** affect the **distribution of population. **
 
• **Climate:**
 
 
• The climate of a region plays a significant role in determining the** distribution of population.**
 
• People tend to settle in areas with **moderate temperatures, adequate rainfall, and comfortable living conditions.**
 
• **Harsh climatic conditions** such as extreme cold or hot weather, frequent natural calamities like floods, hurricanes, or droughts, can make an area **unsuitable** for human habitation.
 
 
 
• **Soil:**
 
 
• The** fertility of soil **determines the type of crops that can be grown in an area, which in turn influences the settlement patterns of people.
 
• Areas with** fertile soil and suitable climate** are likely to have a** higher population density** as they can support agriculture and other related industries.
 
 
 
• **Topography:**
 
 
• Topography refers to the physical features of the land, such as **mountains, valleys, plains, and plateaus.**
 
• People are more likely to settle in areas with** flat land and easy accessibility to water** and other resources.
 
 
 
• **Mountainous regions** may have a** lower population density** due to the difficulty in transportation and limited space for agriculture.
 
• **Water: **
 
 
• Water is a critical resource for **human survival, **and its availability determines the distribution of population.
 
• People tend to settle near water sources like** rivers, lakes, and oceans**, as they provide a source of drinking water, irrigation, and transportation.
 
• Areas with limited water resources may have a** lower population density.**

questions.question: Sanskrit is a part of a family of languages known as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-European.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sanskrit** is a **classical language of India** and is considered to be one of the **oldest languages** in the world.
 
• It belongs to the **Indo-European family of languages,** which also includes languages like** English, Spanish, French, and Hindi.**
 
• Sanskrit has had a significant impact on the development of many other languages, including those in **Southeast Asia and the Middle East.**
 
• The **grammar and structure of Sanskrit** are highly complex and have been studied extensively by** linguists and scholars.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sino-Tibetan,** also known as Trans-Himalayan, is a family of more than **400 languages** with more native speakers than **Indo-European.

 Mandarin, W, Yuè, and Min **are their names.

 
 
• Outside of the Sinitic language family, **Burmese** is the most widely spoken language.
 
 
 
• The **South, South-Central, Central, and North **groupings o**f Dravidian languages** are further broken down into **24 subgroups.**
 
 
• The Indian constitution recognizes **Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, and Kannada** as the country's four principal literary languages.

questions.question: Data Protection Bill 2021 ensures which fundamental right?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Privacy.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Data Protection Bill 2021** ensures the **fundamental right to privacy** for individuals in India.
 
• This right includes the right to control how **personal data** is **collected, processed, and shared** by entities such as government agencies and** private companies.**
 
• The bill also outlines penalties for **violations of this right**, including **fines and imprisonment.**
 
• The right to privacy is recognized as a **fundamental right **in the Indian Constitution under **Article 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right to Freedom of Speech** is also recognized as a **fundamental right** in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 21-A** states that all children between the ages of six and fourteen have the fundamental** right to free and compulsory education.**
 
• A law known as the **Right to Information Act of 2005 (RTI)** was passed by the Indian Parliament "to provide for setting out the practical regime of **right to information **for citizens."

questions.question: Kelucharan Mohapatra is a famous personality associated with which of the following dance forms?

• Kelucharan Mohapatra was born in **1926 **in the state of Odisha and started his dance training at a young age under the guidance of his** guru, Pankaj Charan Das.**
 
• He has received several awards and honors for his contribution to the field of dance, including the **Padma Vibhushan,** the second-highest civilian award in India.
 
• **Kathak, Chhau, and Manipuri **are also prominent Indian classical dance forms, but they are not directly associated with Kelucharan Mohapatra.

• **Manipuri** is a dance form that originated in the **northeastern state of Manipur **and is known for its **fluid and graceful movements.**

questions.question: Which among the following occur when two tectonic plates are moving past each other with different speeds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthquake.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Earthquakes** are caused by the **movement of tectonic plates.**
 
• When two plates move past each other with different speeds, it** creates friction and pressure** that can lead to earthquakes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drought, hurricane, and blizzard** are not caused by the movement of tectonic plates.
 
• **Drought **is typically caused by a** lack of rainfall,** while **hurricanes and blizzards** are** weather events** that are influenced by atmospheric conditions.
 
• **Tectonic plates **are large pieces of the **Earth's crust** that move slowly over time.
 
• They can** collide, move apart, or slide past each other, **creating various geological features such as **mountains, valleys, and volcanoes.**
 
• The movement of tectonic plates can also cause **tsunamis,** which are large waves that can be triggered by **earthquakes or volcanic eruptions.**
 
• Tsunamis can cause significant damage to coastal areas and can be** dangerous to human life.**

questions.question: What is the minimum age a person should be if he/she is willing to be appointed as the Governor of a state in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**35 years.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** minimum age a person** should be if he/she is willing to be appointed as the **Governor of a state** in India is** 35 years.**
 
• This is mentioned in **Article 157 **of the Indian Constitution which states that a person shall not be eligible for appointment as Governor unless he is a **citizen of India** and has completed the **age of 35 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Governor **is the **Constitutional Head of a state** in India and is appointed by the **President of India.**
 
• The Governor's term of office is** five years** but can be** terminated earlier** by the President.
 
• The Governor has many powers and functions such as** administering oaths and affirmations, summoning and proroguing the state legislature, giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature, and appointing judges of the state High Court.**

questions.question: The force exerted by a charged body on another charged or uncharged body is known as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**electrostatic force.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electrostatic force** is the force exerted by a **charged body **on another **charged or uncharged body**.
 
• It is a fundamental force of nature and is responsible for the interaction between **electrically charged particles.**
 
• This force is also known as **Coulomb force,** named after **Charles-Augustin de Coulomb,** who first described it.
 
• The **magnitude of electrostatic force** depends on the **charge of the particles **and the **distance** between them.
 
• **Angular force, pressure, and muscular force** are not related to the interaction between charged particles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Angular force **is the force that causes an object to **rotate **around an axis.
 
• **Pressure** is the** force exerted per unit area** and is related to the distribution of force over a surface.
 
• **Muscular force** is the force exerted by **muscles** and is related to the movement of living organisms.

questions.question: Article 19-22 of the Indian Constitution deals with which of the following fundamental rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Freedom.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 19-22** of the Indian Constitution deals with the **Right to Freedom**, which is a **fundamental right **guaranteed to all citizens of India.
 
• This includes the** freedom of speech and expression**, the **freedom to assemble peacefully**, the **freedom to form associations or unions**, and the** freedom to move freely** throughout the country. 
 
• The Right to Freedom is essential for the **functioning of a democratic society**, as it allows citizens to **express their opinions,** participate in political activities, and hold their government accountable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **freedom of conscience**, as well as the **right to profess, practice, and spread religion**, are guaranteed to all people under **Article 25. **
 
• All forms of **forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking **are forbidden by the **Right against Exploitation.**
 
 
• The terms of this privilege are covered by **Articles 23 and 24.** 
 
 
 
• According to** Article 14 **of the Indian Constitution, "The State shall not deny to any person within the territory of India,** equality before the law** or the equal protection of the laws."

questions.question: During which freedom struggle movement, Mahatma Gandhi Ji gave the call for "Do or Die"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quit India movement.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi Ji** gave the call for **"Do or Die"** during the **Quit India movement.**
 
• The Quit India movement was launched on **8th August 1942**, demanding the immediate** end of British rule** in India.
 
• The movement was a **mass civil disobedience campaign**, and the slogan "Do or Die" was meant to **inspire people** to fight for their freedom.
 
• The movement was **suppressed** by the British authorities, and many leaders including Mahatma Gandhi Ji were **arrested.**
 
• The Quit India movement played a significant role in **India's struggle for independence, **and it was a turning point in India's history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Khilafat movement:**

 
 
• The Khilafat movement was launched in** 1919** to** protest against the disintegration of the Ottoman Empire** and the **abolition of the caliphate.**
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi Ji** supported the movement and it helped to **unite the Muslims and Hindus** in India.
 
 
 
• **Non-cooperation movement:**
 
 
• The Non-cooperation movement was launched in **1920** to **boycott British goods and institutions.**
 
• Mahatma Gandhi Ji called off the movement in **1922** after the **Chauri Chaura incident.**
 
 
 
• **Dandi March:**
 
 
• The Dandi March was a salt march led by Mahatma Gandhi Ji in **1930** to protest against the British salt tax.
 
• The march lasted for **24 days** and covered a distance of **240 miles.**
 
• It was a significant event in** India's struggle for independence.**

questions.question: Every year, Halloween is celebrated on _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**31st October.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Halloween **is celebrated on** 31st October every year.**
 
• It is a festival that originated from** ancient Celtic festival of Samhain, **where people would **light bonfires and wear costumes** to ward off ghosts.
 
• Halloween is primarily celebrated in the **United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom,** but it has also gained popularity in many other countries in recent years.
 
• **Trick-or-treating, carving pumpkins, and attending costume parties** are some of the popular Halloween traditions.
 
• It is a festival celebrated to remember the** dead, **including **saints (hallows), martyrs,** and all the faithful** departed.** 
 
• It is believed that on this day, the** veil** between the living and the dead is at its thinnest, and the **dead can return **to the world of the living.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **24th November** is the date of **Thanksgiving,** which is a **national holiday** celebrated in the **United States and Canada **to give thanks for the blessings of the year. 
 
• **25th December** is the date of **Christmas, **which is a religious and cultural festival celebrated by Christians around the world to commemorate the **birth of Jesus Christ. **
 
• **1st October** is the date of **International Day of Older Persons**, which is observed to raise awareness about the issues affecting elderly people and to promote **their well-being.**

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Biologist who discovered cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Hooke.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Robert Hooke** discovered** cells in 1665** while examining a thin slice of **cork under a microscope.**
 
• **Rosalind Franklin **was a** chemist and X-ray crystallographer** who made significant contributions to the discovery of the** structure of DNA.**
 
• **Gregor Mendel **was an **Augustinian friar and scientist** who is known as the father of modern genetics for his pioneering work in **pea plant breeding.**
 
• **Charles Darwin** was a **naturalist and biologist** who is best known for his** theory of evolution** by natural selection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cells **are the **basic structural and functional units **of living organisms, and the discovery of cells marked a major milestone in the development of modern biology.
 
• Robert Hooke's **discovery of cells **was made possible by the** invention of the microscope**, which allowed scientists to see structures that were too small to be seen with the naked eye.
 
• **Rosalind Franklin's **work on X-ray crystallography was instrumental in the discovery of the **double helix structure of DNA,** but she died before the **Nobel Prize** was awarded to her colleagues James Watson, Francis Crick, and Maurice Wilkins in 1962.
 
• **Gregor Mendel's experiments** with pea plants laid the foundation for the **modern science of genetics, **but his work was largely ignored by the scientific community until the early 20th century.
 
• **Charles Darwin's theory of evolution** by natural selection revolutionized our understanding of the** diversity of life on Earth, **but it was based on observations of living organisms rather than the structure of cells.

questions.question: The Ilbert Bill provided for __________.

options.text: Equality between British and Indian Judges

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Equality between British and Indian Judges.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ilbert Bill **was introduced in **1883 **by **Sir Courtenay Ilbert,** the law member of the **Viceroy's council.**
 
• The main purpose of the bill was to **provide equality between British and Indian judges** in the Indian legal system.
 
• It bears **Courtenay Ilbert's **name because he was the one who first suggested changing the **1861 Indian Criminal Procedure Act** to include it.
 
• This law prohibited **British people** from having their cases heard in courts presided over by **Indian magistrates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The bill faced **opposition **from the British community in India, who were against the idea of Indian judges having the **same powers as British judges**.
 
• The Ilbert Bill's** amendments** lowered the restrictions on these officials, enabling** British subjects** to be tried by **Indian magistrates** who had risen through the ranks of the civil service.
 
• **Lord Ripon**, who had been given specific instructions by British prime minister **William Gladstone** to reserve some of the law's most severe measures for native Indian justices,** backed **the bill.

questions.question: Which among the following plant kingdoms are divided into liverworts and mosses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bryophytes.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **plant kingdom **that is divided into **liverworts and mosses **is **Bryophytes.**
 
• Bryophytes are **non-vascular plants** that do not have **specialized tissues** for the **transport of water and nutrients.**
 
• Bryophytes are **typically small **and prefer **damp locations**, though they can endure in **drier conditions** as well.
 
• There are around **20,000 different plant species** in the bryophytes.
 
• Bryophytes** do not** produce flowers or seeds, but instead **gametangia and sporangia,** which are enclosed reproductive organs. 
 
• They create **gemmae or fragments** to reproduce **asexually or sexually**, respectively, using **spores and spores.**​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pteridophytes** are** vascular plants** that include **ferns and horsetails.**

 
 
• They have **specialized tissues** for the **transport of water and nutrients.**
 
 
 
• **Spermatophyta **are **seed-bearing vascular plants **that include gymnosperms and angiosperms.
 
• **Sphenopsida** are a class of vascular plants that include **horsetails and scouring rushes.**

questions.question: The Gandhisagar dam of Madhya Pradesh is built over which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chambal.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gandhisagar dam** is located in **Mandsaur district of Madhya Pradesh** and is one of the major dams on the **Chambal river.**
 
• The dam was built in **1960** and has a capacity of **8.6 billion cubic meters of water.**
 
• The dam serves the purpose of **irrigation, hydro-electric power generation, **and **flood control.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

• **Kaveri river** is a major river in South India.
 
 
• It originates in the** Western Ghats **and flows through the states of **Karnataka and Tamil Nadu** before emptying into the **Bay of Bengal.**
 
 
 
• **Ravi river **is a major river in **North India.**
